newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms on pending tax, wage payments.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms on pending tax, wage payments.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at 969-973 per mark on Tuesday, up from 976-978 at Monday's close due to higher foreign currency supply from clients ahead of tax and salary payments due by end-month, dealers said.
* The lev gained to 1,670-1,672 per dollar from 1,680-1,684 on Monday, adjusting to the international mark/dollar cross.
* The lev will be pegged at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 to the mark as anchor in a currency board system, to be launched from July 1.
* Dealers expected foreign currency demand from banks and clients to be low today despite falling yields on government securities due to the need for fresh levs for immediate payments.

* The average yield to maturity on four-week discount T-bills, issued daily by the Finance Ministry, fell to 0.47 percent at Monday's auction from 0.58 percent on Friday, 0.62 percent on Thursday and 0.69 on Wednesday.
* Yield to maturity on three-month discount T-bills auctioned on Monday fell to 2.55 percent from 3.80 percent a week earlier. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
